title: It's a bit weird to find and override the previous page hidden class
body:
maybe we can find something easier

![image](https://cloud.githubusercontent.com/assets/976175/11142260/3ff40cee-89ec-11e5-8011-b0948dec929f.png)

comments.body: And I didn't find how to put a disabled attribute on the link instead of hiding it

> And I didn't find how to put a disabled attribute on the link instead of hiding it

Indeed you can't I think because the surrouding link is not a template, only what's inside (label)

it leads to ugly css to do something really basic

![image](https://cloud.githubusercontent.com/assets/976175/11142703/b99ea452-89ef-11e5-90a7-3e7f7443806f.png)

Sorry, not sure I get the issue. Which part do you find ugly? You can remove the `#pagination` selector as this is overspecific, this will make the selector easier to understand. Do you suggest we add a `disabled` class to the link as well as the parent?

The underlying issue I think is that we automatically hide the previous link if you are on first page. If you want to disable this behavior there's no API for that.

We could provide one, works?

Yes, we could provide an option to not mark previous link as disabled.

But I think the issue @Shipow was refering to was more about styling the disabled links with gray color and disabled cursor (for example) instead of hiding them.

That's two different issues.
Yes I don't think hidding the link is the bullet silver so it should be easy to change behavoir.
@Shipow Aside from providing an option to still see the link, you will have to style it. Does adding ais-pagination--link__disabled would work for you?
if default markup is a link `Previous` it's easy to customize/hide

This can definitely be done, but we have the same kind of issues in the refinementList for the active links. 

As a side note, is `.ais-pagination--link__disabled` really needed when we have `.ais-pagination--item__disabled a`?

I'm ok with adding the disabled class to the link in the end, we just need to be consistent with the other widgets.
and you can probably use a[disabled=disabled] but not the most obvious

So, do we need to do something on this one or is it ok?

cc @Shipow
For now .ais-pagination--item__disabled a is sufficient. @Shipow if it's really bothering reopen
